To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

NT‐S100 peptide (NT‐ S100A8), which is released by PC cells and which is elevated in PC patient plasma, is a novel regulator of insulin secretion and PC invasion, and that the effects of NT‐S 100A8 on insulin secretion and PC cell invasion are mediated by the Akt and NF‐kappa B signaling pathways.
NT‐S1008, a peptide isolated from pancreatic cancer (PanCa) tissue, stimulates PanCa cell growth and invasion in vitro, and it enhances insulin secretion and [Ca2+], oscillations from β‐cells.

NT‐S100 peptide induces pancreatic cancer cell growth and invasion, and enhances insulin release and [Cai2+] oscillations of insulin‐secreting cells, and that it does not interfere in insulin signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the role of NT‐S 100A8 on pancreatic cancer and diabetes mellitus, two pathologies which often coexist in the same patient and are both associated to the presence of the S100 family of proteins, in particular S100A8.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of PC‐induced diabetes mellitus, with the final aim of developing a therapeutic approach to this disease
the study of pancreatic cancer (PC), the most common cause of cancer‐associated death from pancreatic cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NT‐S1008 is a novel peptide that can be used to treat pancreatic cancer.
NT‐S1008 is a pro‐diabetogenic peptide that induces pancreatic cancer cell proliferation and invasion, but not insulinoma cell proliferation.

NT‐S1008 induces a rapid insulin release, which in turn induces [Ca2+] oscillations in β‐cells, while NT‐S100 does not interfere with either insulin signaling, or the insulin induced [Ca2+] fluxes, but it induces [Ca2+ ] oscillations and insulin secretion independently of insulin signaling, and it induces a mild growth of PC cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S100A8 is an interesting molecule, which is able to influence pancreatic cell function.
the S100A family of proteins, in particular S100A8, is involved in a number of diseases and disorders, including cancer, diabetes and Alzheimer's Disease, among others.
NT‐S100 is a novel, potent, and selective inhibitor of pancreatic cancer cell invasion and a novel stimulator of insulin release and [ca2+]i oscillation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

S100A8, a protein found in pancreatic cancer tissue, is able to alter the intracellular Ca2+ flux in pancreatic cancer cells and pancreatic islets, which may be a contributing factor to diabetes mellitus in patients with pancreatic cancer.
the N‐terminal peptide of S100A8 (NT‐S 100A8) induces insulin secretion and [Ca2+ ]i oscillations in insulin secreting cells.
the N‐terminal peptide of S100A8 (NT‐S10A8) is able to alter intracellular calcium flux in insulin secreting cells, as well as pancreatic cancer (PC).
